payload.root_cause: In `slugify` at src/text.js:11, the replace regex `/[\s-]+/` is missing the global (`g`) flag. JavaScript's `String.prototype.replace` with a non-global regex replaces only the first match, so only the first whitespace/hyphen run in the title is converted to a dash while subsequent runs are left intact (double spaces preserved). For input 'Hello Big  World!', after lowercase/trim/stripping non-alphanumerics you get 'hello big  world'; only the space after 'hello' is replaced, yielding 'hello-big  world' instead of 'hello-big-world'. The adjacent replaces on lines 10 and 12 correctly use `g`, confirming the intended behavior.

Adding the `g` flag makes every `[\s-]+` run collapse to a single '-', matching the sibling global replaces on lines 10 and 12. Verified against both test cases: 'Hello Big  World!' → 'hello big  world' → 'hello-big-world', and '  Already-slugged  title ' → trim → 'already-slugged  title' → 'already-slugged-title' (after trailing-dash strip, which is a no-op). This is a one-character, single-line change with no side effects on other functions.
